Compactor.description: Internal compaction handoff — do not invoke directly via call_subagent. The checkpoint engine delegates transcript summarization here.

DevOps.description: Verify + release owner — pre-production polisher: run test suites/coverage/regression and report observed results (gate test, security, performance), then production readiness audit and runtime hardening (health/ready probes, structured logging, error tracking, docker/nginx/env docs), installing the tiered CI/security gate (T1 fast-checks / T2 staging / T3 release), branch ladder + protection, and verifying the first run and live URL with observed facts. Not feature work (Dev) or design/browser checks (UI).

Dev.description: Developer — pure implementer: receives specs and tasks from the orchestrator, writes clean tested TDD code, handles errors

Explore.description: Read-only codebase recon — 'where is X defined/used', trace a flow across files, map an unfamiliar subsystem, or gather exact file:line evidence before a plan or a risky edit. Reads and searches only; never edits, builds, or deploys. One focused question per spawn; not implementation (Dev) or browser checks (UI).

FreeAgent.description: General — non-coding life & work assistant: research, documents (PDF/docx/xlsx), planning, web browsing, image understanding, personal admin. NOT a coder — code requests route back to Dev.

General.description: General — non-coding life & work assistant: research, documents (PDF/docx/xlsx), planning, web browsing, image understanding, personal admin. NOT a coder — code requests route back to Dev.

House.description: House — home control specialist: reads and actuates the smart home via house_* tools (lights, climate, locks, plugs, blinds, cameras, scenes). NOT a coder — code requests route back to Dev.

UI.description: Frontend/UI design owner — greenfield UI, redesign, design system, visual direction — and the browser/UI verifier (navigate, click, fill, extract, screenshot). Delivers real frontend artifacts and owns the `## Design` section of .agent-memory/project.md; not for feature work inside an existing design system (Dev does that, following `## Design`).

delegate_description:
Spawn one or more workspace agents (Developer / General / House) IN PARALLEL. Every item gets its own visible chat; final replies arrive as [DELEGATION RESULT] events while you keep coordinating.

BRIEF — you define WHAT, never HOW. Each item carries outcome (what Sir gets when it is done, in Sir's terms) and acceptance (how success will be judged — observable evidence). Never prescribe libraries, frameworks, architecture, step lists, file-by-file plans, or design direction; the specialist is the pro and owns the method (it may deviate and must report deviations). Name a command in acceptance only if Sir named it or it is the project's standard entry point; otherwise describe the behavior and let the specialist choose the proof. One or two lines each — if they get long, you are doing the specialist's job. Method reminders are added to the task automatically; do not write them yourself.

BATCHING — per user turn: put EVERY independent job from the current request into a SINGLE delegate(items=[...]) call. Any agent mix is allowed and runs in parallel — solo scope (just Developer, just General, or just House) or mixed (Developer + General, Developer + House, all three). The sole batching criterion is independence. If job B needs job A's output, do NOT bundle B with A: delegate A first, wait for its [DELEGATION RESULT], then delegate B with A's result in the task. Never split a single request across multiple delegate calls for tidiness or sequencing — one call, all independent items.

EFFORT — match effort to the request: one job for a simple ask, 2-4 for comparisons, more ONLY when directions are truly independent. Jobs beyond the parallel cap wait as 'queued' and start automatically — never flood the system.

RESULTS — each job's final reply arrives as a [DELEGATION RESULT] summary (plus its artifact path and, when set, acceptance). Drill into the full report with delegation_status(id=...) when needed; never paste reports into your reply.

CHAT CONTINUATION — chat_id is optional. Omit it for a new job (default). Set it ONLY when this item is a follow-up, correction, or bug on a chat you can identify from a prior [DELEGATION RESULT] in this session. If the chat_id you pass does not exist, the runtime silently starts a new chat — so never guess an id.

RESUME — project continues a REGISTERED project's durable Dev session instead of starting a new chat. When the request is a follow-up, bug fix, or new work on an EXISTING project and you have no chat_id from a prior [DELEGATION RESULT] in this session, pass project=<name> (agent must be Dev or omitted) instead of workspace/chat_id. The message goes to the project's durable Dev in its own project chat — nothing new is created — and the completion arrives as a [DELEGATION RESULT] like any other job. Unknown names return [NOT FOUND] with the available names — never guess. Omit project for genuinely new work.
delegate_doc: delegate(items=[{agent, task, outcome?, acceptance?, timeout?, title?, chat_id?, project?, workspace?, images?}]) — Spawn Developer/General/House agents; each gets its own chat (project=<name> continues a registered project's durable Dev in its own chat instead). outcome/acceptance define WHAT success is — never method. Results arrive as [DELEGATION RESULT] summaries + artifact paths; drill in with delegation_status(id).
